description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09), while measuring #1247 (b).  PRE-EXISTING.

    $? = 256; print "q=$?\n";
    perl : q=256
    PCL  : q=0

The emission is `(p-scalar-= $? 256)` and `$?` is a plain `(defvar $? 0)`, not
a box, so the assignment does not land where the reader looks.  A status set by
`system`/backticks DOES work (the runtime setfs $? directly), so only the
program's own assignment is lost.

It matters beyond cosmetics: perl's uncaught-die exit status is
`$! || ($? >> 8) || 255`, so the middle branch is reachable in PCL only from a
real child's status.  Row 13 of Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t asserts PCL's current
answer with this task named, so closing this FAILS that row rather than passing
unnoticed.


=== DONE (s495f, 2026-09-25) ===
Fixed with #2009 (one seam): $? is a magic integer box; see #2009 DONE for the design, probes and guards (Pl/t/die-exit-status-01.t rows 13 and 14-23).
subject: SILENT WRONG: `$? = N` does not stick -- an explicit assignment to $? is lost
